title: This sub-$7,000 sportscar might be just what the future needs
gist: A profile of Robert Ely's Gasolini AR1, a sub-$7,000 hand-built single-seat sportscar using a Honda CBR500 motorbike powertrain, presented as a lightweight, efficient antithesis to the excess of million-dollar hypercars at Monterey Car Week.

insights.claim: The Gasolini AR1 is a sub-1,000 lb, 47 hp single-seater built from a 2017 Honda CBR500 motorbike powertrain and Ford Ka wheels, buildable for under $7,000 from purchased plans, returning about 41 mpg.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: A hobbyist counter-thesis to ever-more-powerful, expensive cars; illustrative of enthusiast demand for cheap lightweight vehicles, not an investable trend.

insights.claim: Ely is building an electric AR2 that swaps the motorbike engine for a HyPer 9 motor and Jaguar I-Pace battery cells, with roughly double the horsepower and four times the torque.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Shows the low-cost DIY approach extending to EV powertrains using salvaged parts.
insights.locator: Ely is also working on AR2

insights.claim: Monterey Car Week auctions set records including $42.9 million for a Shelby Daytona Coupe and $40 million for Ferrari's first privately sold Luce EV, framing a market of seven-figure hypercars the author contrasts with cheap fun.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Data point on the collector-car and hypercar market's record valuations.
insights.locator: This past weekend saw Monterey Car Week
